B0549.seeker_flawed_plan: Cian plans to ease his ethical discomfort by asking to be reassigned away from any procedure involving animal handling, assuming that staying in the facility only for record-keeping and cage-side observation keeps him at a clean moral distance from the animal work.
B0549.flaw_explanation: Cage-side observation and record-keeping are still part of the animal-use protocol and often directly affect the animals' care and the study's data, so they do not create the moral separation Cian assumes; a knowledgeable person would note that these tasks are typically covered under the same protocol and oversight as the handling work.

B2209.seeker_flawed_plan: Selah plans to choose quartersawn oak for the sliding lid so that the flat-sawn face of the lid will stay dimensionally stable across its width and slide smoothly regardless of seasonal humidity changes.
B2209.flaw_explanation: Quartersawn lumber is stable across its width, but a sliding lid's critical movement is along the grain direction (length), where all wood species expand and contract very little anyway; the lid's fit is governed by the cross-grain width of the box opening, not the lid's face orientation, so choosing quartersawn stock for the lid does not solve the seasonal binding Selah is worried about.

B2972.seeker_flawed_plan: Pablo plans to pry the old seal out with a flathead screwdriver and then drive the new seal into the gland with a hammer and a socket, figuring that as long as it seats flush it will hold pressure.
B2972.flaw_explanation: Hammering the new seal in dry and slightly cocked will often shave or nick the seal lip and distort the gland bore, so it will leak again almost immediately; seals need to be lubricated and pressed in squarely with a proper seal driver.

B6049.seeker_flawed_plan: Elias plans to sign up for four night-friendly courses this term, reasoning that since each class meets only once a week, the total weekly class time is low enough to fit around his night shifts.
B6049.flaw_explanation: Weekly meeting time is not a measure of workload; each course still requires several hours of reading, assignments, and study outside class, so four courses would likely demand far more total hours than the once-a-week schedule suggests.
